Hi everyone. This is Cascade Legal Rights Project, the organization that runs the free tenant clinic. Thank you to the moderator for inviting us to respond, and thank you to everyone who raised this. Getting a letter from a lawyer right after you've reached out for help is scary, and it makes sense that people want answers.

Our policy prohibits sharing, selling, or disclosing information about clinic attendees. That includes landlords and their attorneys, without exception. Sign-in records stay inside our organization and are kept in locked storage.

Eviction filings in magistrate court are public records. Some law firms and other businesses look up new filings and send mailings to the tenants named in them. If you've received a letter like this soon after a case was filed against you, the court filing is the most likely explanation. It doesn't mean anyone at the clinic shared your information.

We won't discuss anyone's individual situation here, even to explain our side. Everyone who comes to the clinic deserves that privacy. If you're worried about a letter you received, please contact us directly and we'll talk it through with you one on one.

The clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10am to 1pm. The library meeting room is closed that day for HVAC repairs, so we've moved to the Mt Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The side entrance by the parking lot is accessible. It's still free and walk-in, with no appointment needed. Volunteer attorneys and staff will be there to look at eviction notices and court papers and explain your options.

If you've been to a clinic before, or you've never been and you're nervous about coming, you are still welcome.

Questions can go to clinic@cascaderights.example, or you can call our office at 404-555-0187.
